lines.text: Hello, come in, take a seat. I'm Tom, one of the physios.
So, Lorna, what are you coming in with?
I'm coming in with my right knee giving way on the stairs, it's happened three times this month.
And when did it start, the giving way?
It started after the last operation, I've had previous surgery on it twice.
Sorry, three previous surgeries, I forgot the keyhole one when I was nineteen.
Three operations, okay. Do you get any swelling after it gives way?
It puffs up for a day each time if you want to have a look at my photos.
Not sure I've timed it properly, mind.
Let me have a look at the knee. Can you lie back?
There's a small amount of fluid, and when I push the shin forward it moves further than on the left.
The thigh muscle on the right is visibly smaller too, by about two centimetres.
Is that bad? I'm positive it's the cartilage again, my surgeon said so last year.
It might be the ligament rather than the cartilage, I can't be certain without a scan, so I'd like you to see a GP about a referral to the knee team.
Until then, wear the knee brace for stairs and uneven ground, and build the thigh up with the sit to stands we'll go through now.
Okay. Should I stop going to the gym?
Keep going, but stick to the bike and the leg press, nothing with jumping or sudden turns.
Right, let's do those sit to stands before you go.
